correctness.rationale: For B=∏[-a_i,a_i], n>=3 and a1>a2>=...>0, a generic section vertex intersects a box edge. Any section edge parallel to i>=2 has squared norm at least R0^2+(a1^2-a2^2); thus diameters approaching 2R0 isolate the cone with only first-coordinate edge intersections. There R(H)^2=R0^2+(sum_{j>=2}a_j|u_j|/|u1|)^2 exactly. With tau=sqrt(R0 epsilon+epsilon^2/4) the event becomes the weighted (n-1)-dimensional l1-ball sum a_j|y_j|<=tau in projective normal coordinates y_j=u_j/u1. Its Euclidean volume 2^(n-1)tau^(n-1)/((n-1)!product a_j), times spherical density (1+||y||^2)^(-n/2)=1+O_B(tau^2) and two pole charts, gives the displayed prefactor and exponent (n-1)/2 with relative O_B(epsilon). The unique-longest-axis strict gap is essential and tied axes excluded. Independent exact rational edge-intersection test passed 147 representative cases, not an infinite proof.
